text:
elaine: Heads up — BoardCo on Dedicated (dc-us-west-2-pool-A) reported bursty traffic at ~3500 tps around 14:05 PT. They started getting 429s and some 503s. Customer says their app sees token-per-second SLO violations. Ticket #SUP-1129 :rotating_light:

ajay: thx. Any recent config changes to autoscale or admission-control for that pool?

elaine: Not that I can see. Last change was a policy tweak last week but unrelated. Posting admission_control snapshot they shared:
```json
{"pool":"dc-us-west-2-pool-A","tps_limit":2000,"burst_credits":0,"inflight":2100,"queued":420,"drop_rate":0.12}
```

samir: burst_credits:0 stands out — looks like credits exhausted and admission control started rejecting. Do we have history for their credit regen rate?

ajay: pulling metrics — @sre-bot can you paste recent credit regen and scale events?

sre-bot: Credit regen for pool dc-us-west-2-pool-A: 0.6 credits/sec (avg last 1h). Autoscale events: +1 node at 13:50, +0 nodes after. Current headroom (estimated): ~18% under sustained 3k tps.

linda: Customer reports burst was a marketing flash — traffic spiked for ~7m then subsided. They ask for immediate mitigation and plan to avoid in future.

ajay: Immediate mitigations we can try: 1) Temporarily raise tps_limit for that pool (requires approval), 2) Bypass strict admission control for BoardCo by tagging their traffic to a higher-priority route, 3) Allocate short-lived extra burst credits from global pool if available. Which do we want to run?

elaine: Customer asked for minimal disruption. Option 2 sounds best — route them to reserved headroom, if we can create a route quickly. If not, temporary tps_limit bump.

samir: I'm checking quota. We have one spare node in warm pool that can be moved to dc-us-west-2 (can take ~3m). If we move that node + top up credits by 5000 tokens, should remove 429s.

ajay: Steps to reproduce and validate on our side:
1) Replay traffic replay/boardco-burst-2026-03-17 (in staging) using load-tool: `./bin/replay --profile boardco --tps 3500 --duration 7m`
2) Monitor /internal/v1/admission_control/pools/dc-us-west-2-pool-A
3) Watch metrics: burst_credits, inflight, queued, tps_limit

elaine: I'll get BoardCo permission to route test traffic to staging. Also asking them to share truncated logs with request ids.

tier2-support: Filing plan in the incident tracker: SUP-1129 — mitigation: move warm-node + grant 5k burst credits; fallback: increase tps_limit by 25% if immediate routing not possible. Added SLA impact note.

ajay: I'll prepare a short runbook for ops: commands to move warm node, API calls to top up credits, and how to rollback.

samir: Runbook snippets:
```bash
# move warm node to pool
redwoodctl nodes relocate --node-id warm-42 --to-pool dc-us-west-2-pool-A
# top up burst credits (admin only)
redwood-admin credits grant --pool dc-us-west-2-pool-A --amount 5000 --reason "BoardCo emergency"
```

elaine: Thanks. I'll coordinate with the customer and update once they approve. :thumbsup:

ajay: After mitigation we should re-evaluate autoscale policy: increase target headroom for marketing-like workload profiles, and add pre-warming option or higher regen rate for credits. I'll draft recommended policy changes.

linda: Also propose adding a detection rule: if queue > 300 for >1m and burst_credits < 200, trigger automated temp routing to reserved backlog pool.

elaine: noted. I'll include those in customer post-mortem and ops follow-up.

samir: Closing loop later with perf + billing to see if granting extra credits affects customer invoicing and whether we should reimburse.

elaine: Closing for now pending customer approval.
